boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UC Berkeley traditions and superstitions, from academic-good-luck rituals to Big Game week spirit events.

cards.title: Avoid the Memorial Glade seals
cards.subtitle: Memorial Glade · UC Berkeley
cards.notes: Walk around, rather than over, the three university seals in Memorial Glade if you want to follow Cal’s GPA-luck superstition.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition links stepping on a seal with losing the chance at a 4.0.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley identifies the Memorial Glade seals as sacred in campus lore and says stepping on one may jeopardize a 4.0.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus tradition; observe the seals without obstructing pedestrian paths.

cards.title: Rub 4.0 Ball for luck
cards.subtitle: In front of the Campanile · UC Berkeley
cards.notes: After an accidental seal step, visit the stone sphere in front of the Campanile and rub it for the traditional dose of academic luck.
cards.short_summary: The stone sphere is the customary countermeasure to the seal superstition.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley’s student-life guide says students may kiss or rub 4.0 Ball to counter the bad luck of stepping on a university seal.
cards.access_notes: Viewable from the outdoor area in front of Sather Tower; treat the public artwork respectfully.

cards.title: Roll down 4.0 Hill
cards.subtitle: Faculty Glade · UC Berkeley
cards.notes: Use the grassy slope as a good-luck ritual before exams, choosing dry conditions and leaving room for others using the glade.
cards.short_summary: Students roll the hill hoping for a 4.0 semester.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley describes rolling down 4.0 Hill as a well-known student good-luck tradition before midterms or finals.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor lawn activity; use personal judgment about weather, slope conditions, and accessibility.

cards.title: Yell for Hugo before finals
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide finals lore · UC Berkeley
cards.notes: If you hear the call during finals season, join the harmless campus ritual from an appropriate outdoor spot without disrupting study areas.
cards.short_summary: A finals-week shout-out is tied to Cal lore about a former UC president’s dog.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley lists “Yelling for Hugo” among its traditions and reports a campus explanation connecting it with a UC president’s lost dog before finals.
cards.access_notes: Keep voices considerate and follow campus quiet-area rules, especially during finals.

cards.title: Make the Cal script with card stunts
cards.subtitle: California Memorial Stadium · UC Berkeley
cards.notes: At a Cal football game, follow the colored card and cue instructions from the student-section organizers to help form the shared display.
cards.short_summary: Fans turn colored cards into coordinated designs during football games.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley says Cal card stunts originated at the 1914 Big Game and still create designs, including the Cal script, at football games.
cards.access_notes: Requires a game ticket and participation instructions from event organizers.

cards.title: Hear the California Victory Cannon
cards.subtitle: California Memorial Stadium · UC Berkeley
cards.notes: During a home football game, listen for the Rally Committee’s cannon tradition at kickoff, Cal scores, and a Cal victory.
cards.short_summary: The Rally Committee fires the historic cannon as part of football-game ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley states that the California Victory Cannon is fired at the start of each home football game, after each score, and after each victory.
cards.access_notes: Requires a game ticket; expect a loud ceremonial report and follow stadium staff directions.

cards.entity_name: No Red at the Big Game
cards.title: Wear blue and gold, not red
cards.subtitle: Big Game · Cal–Stanford rivalry
cards.notes: For the annual Stanford rivalry game, choose blue, gold, yellow, or white if you want to take part in Cal’s color tradition.
cards.short_summary: Big Game attire carries a specific rivalry signal: avoid Stanford’s red.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley says avoiding red at sporting events is a well-known Cal tradition, especially at the Big Game, when students choose blue, gold, yellow, and white.
cards.access_notes: Participation is optional; the game itself requires appropriate event admission.

cards.title: Gather for the Big Game Bonfire Rally
cards.subtitle: Hearst Greek Theatre · UC Berkeley
cards.notes: Attend the Rally Committee’s pre-Big-Game program at the Greek Theatre and follow venue guidance around its professionally managed fire display.
cards.short_summary: The eve-of-game rally combines student performances, speakers, and a major bonfire show.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley describes the Bonfire Rally as the Rally Committee’s largest event, held at the Greek Theatre on the eve of the Big Game.
cards.access_notes: Event availability and admission arrangements vary by year; follow official event and venue instructions.

cards.title: Watch the Tree Chopping Rally
cards.subtitle: Big Game Week · UC Berkeley
cards.notes: During Big Game Week, watch UCB Logging race on the paired Cal and Stanford logs; stay in designated spectator areas.
cards.short_summary: A log-chopping race serves as a playful Big Game predictor.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley’s Rally Committee tradition guide describes the Tree Chopping Rally as a Big Game Week event in which UCB Logging races to chop through paired Cal and Stanford logs.
cards.access_notes: Spectate only; do not enter the work area or handle tools unless authorized by organizers.

cards.title: Spot the Big Game cable car rally
cards.subtitle: San Francisco · Big Game Week
cards.notes: Look for the Cal spirit groups’ cable-car ride during Big Game Week, and enjoy it from a safe public viewing point along the route.
cards.short_summary: Selected Cal spirit groups take a cable car through San Francisco to spread school spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley’s Rally Committee guide identifies the Cable Car Rally as a Big Game Week tradition in which Cal spirit groups ride a San Francisco cable car.
cards.access_notes: Participation is limited to selected spirit-group members; public viewers should follow transit and street-safety rules.
